paper.title_en: Phase robust bounds on dark photon production in \(D^{0}\rightarrow\gamma A'\) near the \(\phi\) resonance
paper.abstract_en: A kinetically mixed dark photon produced in <math display="inline"><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>γ</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> probes the timelike electromagnetic current at <math display="inline"><msup><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mn>2</mn></msubsup></math>, where resolved vector-meson structure can render a pointlike continuation from the real photon point inadequate. The magnitudes of the <math display="inline"><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msup></math> and <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> pole residues are normalized to measured radiative charm data and electronic vector-meson widths, while the <math display="inline"><mi>ω</mi></math> contribution is bounded using the experimental upper limit on <math display="inline"><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>γ</mi><mi>ω</mi></math>. Treating the parity conserving and parity violating amplitudes as a complex vector with two components, norm inequalities yield a lower envelope valid for arbitrary relative phases and orientations in this amplitude space once an upper bound on the smooth remainder is specified. At the <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> pole, the combined ceiling of the explicit non-<math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> poles amounts to only 1.93% of the <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> pole amplitude norm for the central inputs. Consequently, complete cancellation at resonance requires the smooth remainder to reach at least 98.1% of the peak <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> pole amplitude norm within the adopted pole decomposition. For the representative <math display="inline"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> benchmark, which bounds the norm of the smooth remainder by half the peak <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> pole amplitude, the conditional floor of the reduced branching fraction at resonance is <math display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mrow></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>low</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.8</mn><msubsup><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>0.14</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.13</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. The corresponding lower envelope remains positive within approximately <math display="inline"><mo>±</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>MeV</mi></math> of the <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> pole. At resonance, this <math display="inline"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> benchmark floor exceeds the pointlike comparison baseline, normalized to the experimental upper limit on <math display="inline"><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>γ</mi><mi>γ</mi></math>, by a factor of <math display="inline"><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.23</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.23</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. These results demonstrate that resolved hadronic structure can substantially affect dark photon production near the <math display="inline"><mi>ϕ</mi></math> resonance.
